properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 1 at 1:24AM CDT until October 2 at 1:00AM CDT by NWS Des Moines IA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Much of central Iowa.

* WHEN...Through late tonight.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Area creeks and streams are running high and could flood with more
heavy rain.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Moderate to heavy rain is ongoing over much of Iowa and is
expected to continue through the morning. Soils are already
saturated, with more rainfall on the way. Rainfall totals will
range from 2 to 4 inches in a southwest to northeast oriented
band across central Iowa, with locally higher amounts likely.
Another push of 1 to 2 inches of rainfall is expected across
southern and southeastern Iowa through mid- day today. This
rainfall may lead to flash flooding. Poor drainage and low lying
areas may experience ponding.

Significant rises are expected or ongoing on many rivers and
streams, which may exceed flood stage. Some larger river basins
of most concern include the South Skunk River basin from Ames
downstream, the Des Moines River basin Des Moines downstream, the
Raccoon River downstream of U.S. Hwy 30, as well as the North,
Middle, South, Nishnabotna, Grand and Chariton River basins.
properties.instruction:

Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

weather.gov/desmoines/water.

* WHEN...From 1 PM CDT this afternoon through early Thursday morning.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Creeks and streams may rise out of their banks.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

develop over portions of Upton and eastern Pecos counties this

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued September 30 at 5:45AM CDT until October 2 at 1:00AM CDT by NWS San Angelo TX
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of west central Texas, including the following
counties, Brown, Callahan, Coke, Coleman, Concho, Crockett, Fisher,
Haskell, Irion, Jones, Kimble, Mason, McCulloch, Menard, Nolan,
Runnels, San Saba, Schleicher, Shackelford, Sterling, Sutton,
Taylor, Throckmorton and Tom Green.

* WHEN...Through late Thursday night.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- There is an increased danger to lives and property due to flash
flooding. Flash flooding is likely and considerable flash
flooding is possible.

- Multiple rounds of heavy rain are possible through Thursday night
as an influx of tropical moisture arrives. This will coincide
with an approaching upper level low pressure system and an
associated frontal boundary. High precipitable water values will
support efficient rainfall production with this activity. Showers
and thunderstorms capable of producing rainfall totals in the 2
to 4 inch range are forecast across the watch area. Locally
higher amounts of 8+ inches care possible.

- Http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
